title: Edera's Object Capability Bounded Authority Promises to Isolate Credentials From AI Agent Workloads
summary:
Edera announced Object Capability Bounded Authority, a security model that separates an AI agent's or MCP server's required authority from the credentials behind it. Hypervisor-enforced capabilities limit agents to specific actions without storing secrets in the workload. Initial releases cover scoped command execution and workload identity; credential-brokered API access will follow.

By Olimpiu Pop

title: Google Cloud API Gateway Introduces Streaming Support for Real-Time and AI-Powered Applications
summary:
Google has announced the public preview of streaming support for API Gateway, extending its traditional request-response model to support applications requiring real-time communication. According to Google, this is particularly relevant for AI applications that provide streaming model responses, multi-step agent workflows, and interactive sessions.

By Sergio De Simone

title: Building a Culture for a Kubernetes-Based Platform in a Bank
summary:
In banking, open source can earn trust by running real workloads, as Marcy Paramonova and Stéphane Cusin explained in their talk Building Cloud Native Culture in a Bank at KubeCon & CloudNativeCon Europe. Deploying Kubernetes was the easy part; the hard part was culture: community of practice, shared knowledge, rituals, ownership. Teams try things, keep what works, and improve bottom-up.

By Ben Linders

title: Presentation: Zero Trust Agent Systems that Pass Audits and Still Ship
summary:
Advait Patel shares a playbook for securing AI agent systems in production. He discusses moving defense boundaries from the prompt to the tool layer, enforcing scoped workload identities, and mitigating prompt injection via tool outputs. He explains how to structure audit-ready observability and implement kill switches to protect critical data while keeping deployment fast and compliant.

By Advait Patel

title: Inkitt Builds a One-Shot PR Creator with Resumable Agent Orchestration
summary:
Inkitt built a one-shot pull request creator that automates small, low-risk code changes from task intake to draft PR creation. Its event-driven orchestrator persists workflow state, coordinates short-lived coding agent containers, bounds retries, and enforces permission restrictions while retaining human review and approval before changes can be merged.

By Leela Kumili

title: Amazon ECS Gateway Arrives with Generated Hostnames and No Custom Domain Support
summary:
AWS has released Amazon ECS Gateway, an account-level ingress resource letting platform teams define networking once and application teams opt services in with a connector. Each service gets a generated hostname and routing is host-based, and neither the announcement nor the documentation covers custom domains.

By Steef-Jan Wiggers

title: Article: The App Is Just the Tip: What It Takes to Build Mobile Infrastructure at Scale
summary:
What determines whether your app feels fast, ships often, and stays stable at scale is not the app itself. It is what sits behind it. This article is about that layer: what it does, why it exists, what it takes to design it correctly, and what happens when you try to migrate a live, high-traffic product onto it without a safety net.

By Kirill Sokolov

title: Docker Urges Isolation and Governance for AI Agent Security
summary:
Docker has published a guide to five security risks that arise when AI agents are allowed to browse, run code and call tools with limited human oversight. They argue that the autonomy that makes agents useful also makes conventional application security controls insufficient. The company positions isolation and governance, rather than model improvements alone, as the main defences.

By Matt Saunders

summary:
Google has introduced the LiteRT Tensor API, a lightweight C++ API that allows developers to build, customize, and optimize machine learning models directly for on-device execution. According to Google, it combines the flexibility of native model authoring with cross-platform portability.

title: Vitest 5: Prioritises Performance with a Shared Vite Server, Trace View, and Stricter Test Defaults
summary:
Vitest 5.0 focuses on speed, with reported gains of 8 to 25 percent in most setups and up to 53 percent in VM pools. It adds a vitest doctor command, Browser Mode Trace View, and vi.when. Defaults are stricter: clearMocks is true and unawaited async assertions fail. It requires Vite 6.4 and Node.js 22.12 or newer.

By Daniel Curtis

title: Google and Meta Open-Source TorchTPU to Bring Native PyTorch Support to Google TPUs
summary:
TorchTPU is an open-source project developed by Google in collaboration with Meta that provides a native PyTorch backend for Google TPUs. It enables PyTorch workloads to execute on TPU hardware with minimal code modifications, supporting eager and compiled execution, distributed computing, and hardware-specific optimizations.

By Sergio De Simone
